After going through a hell of a time in the past few years of my life, I've (somewhat ironically) semi recently rediscovered a connection with God (for lack of a better term?), though it is very personal and I don't really attribute any man made religion to it. Except I say a quiet prayer with myself and God each night. That said, I was born into a catholic family, baptised etc. but growing up, other than some time in a catholic school when I was a child, there wasn't really active practice of religion in my family besides the occasional old tradition. I recall reading the family Bible when I was growing up and having a few discussions with my father about it. He encouraged me to learn about it and explore other religions but when I directly asked why we didn't he explained how he grew up in a strongly Catholic family until his mother (my grandmother whom I never met) died when he was quite young (teenager iirc). This hit the family hard and coupled with a few other bad experiences he said he had no more time left for the church.

Yet despite the many flaws of the Church and disagreements in some areas, I find myself drawn back to Catholicism for some reason. Perhaps a desire for a stronger sense of belonging or community which I've missed since living more in the city rather than rural. I've looked up info on local churches and certain prayers etc. I don't see myself becoming a fanatic or anything but I do find myself becoming more curious and slowly fostering a desire towards getting involved.

I had a few questions and wondering if anyone can answer them. I'm currently on the fence about actually seeking further involvement with any religion hence why I thought I'd ask here first. Forgive me if I seem ignorant, but I'm really just unaware of some of the basics.

As far as I can recall I was never "confirmed" and curious as to what the ceremony is about and what the importance is? (just a coming of age thing or?)

How likely is it to get face to face time with a priest working at a church to ask these kinds of curious questions?

Do I just walk in any time, or go to a Sunday Mass and seek counsel afterwards, or do I try and set up an appointment?

I'm likely interested in getting involved in volunteer work again soon and just wondering which types of things others have found the most rewarding?

Returning or rediscovering faith, a few questions...

How are you doing today? Reading what you've posted, it sounds like yours was one of the many long time Catholic families that left the church following the Vatican 2 council. I imagine there's an unspoken and rich history to be learned there as well. If possible, talk to your father and ask him if he has any of his parents religious effects. Maybe a family bible, rosary, or any other items that could have heirloom significance to your family. Be honest and let him know that you're curious to learn more about the faith and you'd like to know family history as well.

In regards to confirmation, Rite of Christian Initiation of Adults (RCIA) is the class you'll need to complete to be confirmed. They'll cover everything you need to know there. The Catholic Directory dot com has an extensive online director of catholic parishes with contact information if you don't know where to find the parish nearest you. Depending on what city you live in expect to find the non-English mass will have higher attendance than the English mass, but you shouldn't let that deter you from attending a non-English mass. Face time with a priest may vary, sometimes he keeps static office hours, while other times they may reserve for appointments. Also, find out if the parish hosts a National Fellowship of Catholic Men. If you're unable to find one, consider a catholic fraternal organization such as the Knights of Columbus or the Knights of Peter Claver.
